Chapter 1
Introduction to PP/DS with
SAP S/4HANA
To start our journey through production planning and detailed schedul-
ing (PP/DS), we’ll begin with the basics: What is production planning,
what is detailed scheduling, and how have they changed with
SAP S/4HANA?
SAP’s enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, in its different forms, is widely used
by companies around the world across different industries. The various releases of the
software over the years have culminated in the latest two supported releases: SAP ERP
and SAP S/4HANA (the focus of this book). SAP ERP supports many relational databases
from different vendors, whereas SAP S/4HANA is the latest version, tailored for SAP
HANA (the in-memory database created by SAP) and offering many new features.
Since the earliest releases of SAP ERP, SAP has provided solutions for production plan-
ning, capacity, and scheduling resources. In the SAP ERP software, tools such as sales
and operations planning (S&OP), demand management, master production schedul-
ing (MPS), material requirements planning (MRP), capacity scheduling, and leveling
enable the production planning and scheduling functions.
As businesses and manufacturing processes evolved, a need emerged for more com-
plex planning and scheduling algorithms to tackle such complexities. In response, SAP
introduced SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, which later became part of the
SAP Supply Chain Management (SAP SCM) suite. With SAP Advanced Planning and
Optimization, the demand planning, supply network planning, and PP/DS tools were
introduced to solve complex forecasting, planning (long-term, mid-term, and short-
term), and scheduling challenges. With the evolution of the SAP Integrated Business
Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP) cloud solution, support was provided for S&OP,
demand planning, and supply and response planning. SAP IBP is the long- to medium-
term demand and supply planning tool.
In the SAP ERP suite on SAP HANA and, later, in SAP S/4HANA, the classic MRP solution
was enhanced with the power of SAP HANA to perform the complex MRP calculations
in the SAP HANA database layer, thus making multiplying the speed of access to the
MRP results. In combination with the forecasting and long- to medium-term planning
capabilities of SAP IBP, MRP Live in SAP S/4HANA is the solution for short-term plan-
ning.

1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA
20
In 2016, SAP released the 1610 version of SAP S/4HANA software, and the PP/DS compo-
nent of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization was made available within the SAP
S/4HANA core as PP/DS. This enables the SAP S/4HANA solutions capability not only to
support the short-term planning via MRP Live but also to support advanced planning
algorithms and detailed scheduling. Over the years, SAP also made enhancements to
the existing functionalities and introduced new functionalities in SAP IBP and embed-
ded PP/DS.
The SAP digital supply chain is part of the SAP intelligent suite. SAP IBP and PP/DS in
SAP S/4HANA are key components of the plan and manufacture components of the
design-to-operate process within the digital supply chain.
In 2020, SAP also introduced the SAP Digital Supply Chain version of capabilities such
as PP/DS, extended warehouse management (EWM), transportation management, and
so on, in the SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA system.
The SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, offers the capa-
bility of having the SAP Digital Supply Chain system as a hub system for the previously
mentioned capabilities and connecting to multiple ERP systems such as SAP ERP or
SAP S/4HANA. If there are multiple SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA systems in the solution
landscape, these systems can integrate with SAP Digital Supply Chain Management,
edition for SAP S/4HANA, to centrally plan and schedule production. The planning and
scheduling results from SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA,
are sent to the corresponding ERP system. The master data and transaction data
between the SAP Digital Supply Chain system and the corresponding ERP system lever-
age the core interface.
In this chapter, we’ll introduce the concept of PP/DS using SAP systems. We’ll also show
how the solution landscape evolved over time, the deployment options available prior
to SAP S/4HANA, and the simplifications made in PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA compared to
the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. Then, we’ll transi-
tion into the detailed architecture of PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA.
1.1 What Is Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling?
SAP provides tools to support complete supply chain planning and execution, as well
as integration with other processes and areas. One of the core processes within the sup-
ply chain is production planning. The primary objective of production planning is to
ensure that the right product is available at the right time and the right place to be
delivered to customers and ensure the raw materials are available for production.
Detailed scheduling supports the sequencing and scheduling of production operations
by taking into consideration the available resource (machine resources and human
resources) capacity and the availability of materials. In addition, detailed scheduling is
used to ensure the optimal usage of resources.

21
1.1 What Is Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling?
Let’s take a closer look at each in the following sections.
1.1.1 Production Planning
The production planning process involves several steps. Let’s walk through the tradi-
tional flow in SAP ERP, as follows:
1. Sales and operations planning (S&OP)
The production planning process starts with an aggregated sales forecast in S&OP,
which can be disaggregated and then transferred to demand management where it
will become a concrete production plan with a planning strategy defined.
2. Master production scheduling (MPS)
This production plan will be the input for MPS, which is used to plan finished prod-
ucts and products using bottleneck resources. MPS will generate planned orders to
cover the forecast by using different planning parameters for each material, but it
won’t consider capacity restrictions.
3. Capacity leveling
After the MPS execution, capacity leveling should be executed for the generated
planned orders, adjusting the planned order dates and ensuring that the production
plan is feasible and won’t exceed the capacity available in the work centers.
4. Material requirements planning (MRP)
When all capacity issues are solved, it’s time to execute MRP to plan the remaining
products. MRP will generate planned orders to produce semifinished products and
purchase requisitions to procure raw materials.
Even though SAP ERP offers this complete process for production planning, there are
some limitations with the tools offered. For example, materials planning and capacity
leveling are two separated steps: MPS or MRP will first generate planned orders with an
infinite capacity, and the system will only consider finite capacity restrictions during
capacity leveling. Another limitation is that MPS and MRP won’t consider the expira-
tion date of material batches, so the expiration must be controlled separately. These
limitations are in place because these very complex planning scenarios would con-
sume additional hardware resources during the planning run and could require more
time to finish it. In addition, no optimizations are available for planning the produc-
tion or the resource usage on the manufacturing shop floor.
SAP S/4HANA is basically an evolution of SAP ERP, and many of the older features are
being redesigned or even replaced by new features. Although most of these older fea-
tures are still in SAP S/4HANA, they are part of what is called the compatibility scope,
which means they aren’t considered future technology and should be retired in the
future.

1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA
22
Note
When a new SAP S/4HANA release is launched, SAP delivers a document called the sim-
plification list, which describes the major changes of the new release, including the
features that are part of the compatibility scope. An SAP Note linking to the simplifica-
tion list can be found in Appendix A.
In SAP S/4HANA, S&OP and demand management are gradually being replaced by
cloud-based SAP IBP, and capacity planning is being replaced by PP/DS. Production
planning in SAP S/4HANA is powered by MRP Live and forms the production planning
part of PP/DS. PP/DS also offers optimization of the production plan and capacity utili-
zation, including optimized sequencing of orders in the manufacturing resources.
1.1.2 Detailed Scheduling
After the production planning process is complete, resulting in the production propos-
als for the in-house manufactured products, the next step is to identify the correct
resources needed to execute the orders in the manufacturing shop floor where the
detailed scheduling processes are used. The detailed scheduling tools should consider
the availability of the materials for manufacturing and the available capacity of the
machinery, tools, and human resources.
In SAP ERP, detailed scheduling is supported in the form of capacity planning, which
comprises two major features: capacity evaluation and capacity leveling. Capacity
planning supports long-term rough-cut planning, medium-term planning, and short-
term detailed planning.
Capacity requirements are created by orders that are generated via the production
planning tools, such as MPS and MRP. In addition, capacity requirements are created by
networks in project systems and plant maintenance orders. The orders created by the
planning tools are scheduled on the resources (also called work centers) based on the
planning settings and using the routing master data. The routing master data defines
the calculation of the duration for scheduling and the capacity required to execute a
specific manufacturing step.
After the capacity requirements are created, the capacity evaluation tool can be used to
analyze the capacity load on the resources based on the available capacity. The capacity
leveling tools are also used to dispatch and deallocate operations on the resources
based on the underload and overload situations.
For complex manufacturing scenarios, the SAP ERP capacity planning tools have chal-
lenges in optimizing the capacity use of the resources and adhering to the production
schedule to minimize delays in manufacturing. These complex requirements for
capacity planning and detailed scheduling are addressed in the PP/DS component of
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization.

23
1.2 PP/DS with SAP
1.2 PP/DS with SAP
To address those complex planning and scheduling scenarios, SAP created a new PP/DS
tool, as mentioned previously. This tool was introduced a long time ago as part of SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization, which provides a set of advanced supply chain
planning tools. Additionally, SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization could be inte-
grated into one or multiple ERP systems, planning an entire supply chain together. SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization has the special dedicated SAP liveCache data-
base, which was designed to handle very complex algorithms.
The objective of PP/DS is to cover the demand with procurement proposals in the
short-term horizon for critical products or to create an optimized production plan con-
sidering various costs that may influence the production plan—storage costs,
resource/work center costs, and delay penalties—and create an optimized resource
schedule for the resources in which the manufacturing operations are performed.
Key features in PP/DS include the following:
 Production planning heuristics
 Production planning optimizer
 Interactive planning tools
 Detailed scheduling heuristics
 Detailed scheduling optimizer
 Interactive detailed scheduling tools
 Background planning and scheduling tools
 Planning procedures
 Pegging relationships
 Alert Monitor
PP/DS supports various manufacturing processes leveraged by many industries:
 Discrete manufacturing
In industries such as industrial machinery manufacturing, consumer goods, and so
on, the discrete manufacturing process is leveraged in SAP ERP systems. With dis-
crete manufacturing, the production steps flow through multiple workstations
where activities such as assembly are performed, followed by the final product rolling
off the production shop floor. In SAP ERP systems, discrete manufacturing is sup-
ported by routing as the main master data object for the definition of the manufac-
turing steps. The execution of the manufacturing is driven by production orders. In
PP/DS, the discrete manufacturing master data and production orders are supported
to arrive at an optimal production plan and an optimal schedule for the orders.
 Production planning for process industries
The process industry manufacturing process is used by industries such as chemicals,
pharmaceuticals, and food and beverage. The manufacturing process is driven via

1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA
24
material flows and processing of the input materials throughout the process to pro-
duce the final product. In process industry processes, the master recipe is the pri-
mary master data object to define the manufacturing process. The execution object
in the ERP system is called the process order. In PP/DS, specific features such as tank
planning, campaign planning, and continuous input/output planning support the
process industry requirements.
 Repetitive manufacturing
In both discrete-based and process industry-based manufacturing, the manufactur-
ing is driven by production and process orders. In repetitive manufacturing, how-
ever, production is based on the rate in which the production line can produce the
goods. Industries such as electronic/automobile components manufacturing, the
same steps are performed repeatedly throughout a set period until the desired pro-
duction quantity is achieved. So, in repetitive manufacturing, no manufacturing
orders are used and the manufacturing quantity is guided by the planned orders.
But the actual manufacturing will happen based on the rate of production of the
manufacturing line. The requirements in repetitive manufacturing industries, such
as creation of planned orders per period (shift, day, week, etc.) on specific production
lines, are supported by special planning algorithms in PP/DS.
PP/DS also supports certain industry-specific features, such as length-based planning
required for metal industries, and model mix planning, which is widely used in the
automobile industry.
1.2.1 SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization
In this section, we’ll take a closer look at the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Plan-
ning and Optimization, see how it’s embedded in SAP S/4HANA, and walk through how
PP/DS fits into SAP S/4HANA deployment and architecture.
With the SAP S/4HANA 1610 release, PP/DS was made available in the SAP S/4HANA
core. In addition, a side-by-side usage of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization is
possible with SAP S/4HANA as the ERP system.
SAP introduced the cloud-based SAP IBP solution with capabilities such as demand
planning, supply and response planning, and inventory planning, which will replace
the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system for advanced planning and opti-
mization functionalities such as demand planning and supply network planning.
Therefore, the target architecture for the end-to-end planning and scheduling solution
is to have SAP IBP as the demand and supply planning solution and SAP S/4HANA as
the PP/DS system for critical products and components.
Whether it’s SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the configuration data, such as organizational
structures and master data objects (e.g., material master, bill of materials [BOM], rout-
ings, production version, work centers or resources, capacities, vendors, and custom-
ers) are maintained in the ERP system. These data objects are transferred to the SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization system via the core interface.
© 

25
1.2 PP/DS with SAP
Let’s walk through the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization basics, before com-
paring it to PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA (embedded PP/DS).
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization with SAP ERP
In the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, the processes start with
demand planning, where the historical sales and consumption data is used for forecast-
ing the demand. The outcome of demand planning is the constrained forecast, which is
used to perform supply planning. Supply planning is executed using supply network
planning, which comprises complex algorithms in the form of heuristics and the opti-
mizer to plan supplies against demand. Demand planning and supply network planning
are executed for mid- to long-term horizons. The data and process flow between the SAP
ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems is shown in Figure 1.1.
Figure 1.1 Planning Process and Data Flow between SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and
Optimization Systems
For the short-term planning horizon, procurement proposals from the supply plan in
supply network planning are transferred to PP/DS. Within PP/DS, the plan is refined
further.
Comparing the PP/DS component’s capabilities in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi-
zation with the tools available for planning in SAP ERP reveals that the basic structure
behind the two solutions is similar; however, PP/DS provides advanced tools and fea-
tures that aren’t available in SAP ERP, such as the following:
 Materials planning and finite capacity planning
 Optimization of production plan
 Planning with exact times

 Forecast consumption with descriptive characteristics

Some of these features are only possible in the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced
Planning and Optimization, which uses the SAP liveCache database, designed to algo-
rithmically handle complex data and runtime-intensive functions. SAP liveCache is an
object-based and enhanced SAP MaxDB database.
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization connects directly with SAP ERP, and data is
transferred though the core interface. For each piece of master data to be transferred
from SAP ERP to SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization via the core interface, you’ll
need to create and activate an integration model so that the master data can be sent
through the integration queues. After planning in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi-
zation, the planning results are also integrated into SAP ERP via the core interface, and
any record stuck in the integration queue can lead to major integration problems
between the systems or data inconsistencies.
In planning scenarios where there are planning runs to be executed in different sys-
tems, namely, SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, multiple plan-
ning executions are involved, and a lot of dependencies are created due to the same
product getting planned in multiple locations, For example, if the supply chain net-
work consists of three plants—plants 1 and 3 planned in the PP/DS component in SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization and plant 2 planned in the SAP ERP system—and
the product structure extends throughout these three plants, then three different plan-
ning runs need to be spread across the SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Opti-
mization systems. In addition, the second and third planning runs need to wait for the
planning results to be transferred to SAP ERP from SAP Advanced Planning and Opti-
mization and vice versa.
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization versus SAP S/4HANA
Embedded PP/DS brings the PP/DS features from SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi-
zation into the SAP S/4HANA system, enabling the SAP S/4HANA system to act as a
comprehensive planning and scheduling solution for the short-term planning horizon.
From a usability perspective, all PP/DS transactions are available within the SAP S/4HANA
system, allowing end users to perform all the planning and scheduling functions in one
system. With the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, users
need to switch between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and SAP ERP sys-
tems to accomplish the planning and scheduling tasks. In SAP S/4HANA, new SAP Fiori
© 

27
1.2 PP/DS with SAP
apps have been introduced for detailed scheduling that work seamlessly with the SAP
Fiori apps delivered for MRP Live planning.
With SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, the master data and transaction data
need to be transferred between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and SAP
ERP systems because both systems need to be in sync in terms of master data. In addi-
tion, for certain master data fields that are only relevant for SAP Advanced Planning
and Optimization planning, the data is directly maintained only in the SAP Advanced
Planning and Optimization system. The master data also needs to be synced up fre-
quently between the SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems
to ensure that the data is consistent and that the planning results are correct in the SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization system.
In SAP S/4HANA, master data maintenance is greatly simplified by maintaining only
one version of data for SAP S/4HANA as well as for embedded PP/DS. For most master
data objects, there is no need to create an integration model and transfer the data from
SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. Master data objects such as materials and work cen-
ters are maintained in SAP S/4HANA transactions and are flagged for use in advanced
planning.
Note
Advanced planning is the term used in SAP S/4HANA to identify the objects and pro-
cesses that use the PP/DS capability.
The fields relevant to PP/DS fields are also exposed to the SAP S/4HANA master data
objects and can be maintained in one transaction. When the data is stored in the data-
base tables, it’s saved only in SAP S/4HANA tables, and data duplication is avoided
wherever applicable.
Similarly, transaction data such as planned independent requirements (PIRs), planned
orders, production and process orders, purchase requisitions and orders, and sales
orders are transferred to embedded PP/DS without any need for an active integration
model. The relevant transaction data objects are marked as relevant for transfer in Cus-
tomizing, and if the corresponding master data object is also marked as active for
advanced planning, the transaction data is transferred to embedded PP/DS and from
SAP S/4HANA, and vice versa. Because embedded PP/DS also uses SAP liveCache, the
order objects need to be re-created in SAP liveCache upon transfer to embedded PP/DS.
In scenarios involving multiple locations that require MRP and advanced planning,
just one MRP Live planning run in SAP S/4HANA can plan all the materials and loca-
tions, including those in PP/DS. There is no need to set up separate PP/DS planning
runs to generate the procurement proposals for the advanced planning material loca-
tions. The planning run results are synced between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS
in real time, so the risk with the core interface queue failures are greatly reduced.

1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA
28
Note
Although most of the planning and scheduling features are available in embedded PP/DS,
certain features of the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization
aren’t available in embedded PP/DS. The critical simplification items are covered in the
next section, and the complete list is available in SAP Note 3087008.
Embedded PP/DS with SAP IBP
The cloud-based SAP IBP) solution replaces the demand planning and supply network
planning functionalities of the SAP SCM/SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization
solution. SAP IBP also has other integrated solutions such as S&OP and inventory plan-
ning. The long-term supply planning and midterm operational planning happens
within SAP IBP, and the detailed production planning for the shorter planning horizon
happens within embedded PP/DS. So, it’s essential to integrate the supply planning
results from SAP IBP to embedded PP/DS to further fine-tune the plan and to ensure
optimal scheduling of the plan.
The concept of synchronous planning was introduced in SAP IBP and in embedded PP/DS
to provide a flexible integration of the supply plan from SAP IBP into SAP S/4HANA and
the production plan along with the optimized production scheduling results back to
SAP IBP from SAP S/4HANA. The synchronous planning process will also define the
responsibility of the SAP IBP and PP/DS systems in terms of the planning horizons each
of the systems are responsible for.
In SAP IBP, supply planning can be performed in two stages: (1) the time series–based
supply planning is a bucket-oriented planning, where the supply elements are calcu-
lated in periodic buckets (weekly, monthly, etc.); and (2) the SAP IBP response planning
is an order-based supply planning process, where planned orders and purchase requisi-
tions are created considering the lot size and selection of the appropriate source of sup-
ply. Typically, the time series–based supply planning is performed for a longer
planning horizon (e.g., 24 months, in weekly buckets), and the order-based response
planning is performed for the midterm planning horizon (e.g., 3 months). Within the
shorter planning horizon (e.g., 1 month), the response planning results from SAP IBP
are fine-tuned considering the detailed planning and scheduling constraints defined in
embedded PP/DS.
SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, is a new offering to
handle complex solution landscape requirements. For example, if your landscape con-
sists of many ERP systems, including SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA systems, to leverage
PP/DS functionalities, you can only leverage them in the SAP S/4HANA systems as they

1.2 PP/DS with SAP
have the embedded PP/DS solution as part of the SAP S/4HANA core. For the SAP ERP
systems, you still must have an SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system in
the landscape to leverage PP/DS functionalities.
In addition, with your ERP system landscape transformation from SAP ERP systems to
SAP S/4HANA, if you still choose to have a system landscape consisting of multiple SAP
S/4HANA systems to leverage the PP/DS functionalities, the PP/DS setup—including the
installation and management of SAP liveCache—needs to be performed in all those SAP
S/4HANA systems. To reduce the complexity of managing each individual system with
its own SAP liveCache, SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA,
offers a hub solution.
With this, multiple SAP ERP and/or SAP S/4HANA systems can be integrated into one
SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, system for leveraging
PP/DS functionalities. Different flavors of SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edi-
tion for SAP S/4HANA, are available for solution capabilities such as SAP Extended Ware-
house Management (SAP EWM) and SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). SAP
Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA includes a key capability
that supports PP/DS, called SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling.

1.2.2 Key Simplifications in PP/DS for SAP S/4HANA
In this section, we’ll cover the key differences between the features of the PP/DS com-
ponent of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and the embedded PP/DS fea-
tures. These simplification items are dependent on the release version of SAP S/4HANA
(this book is based on the on-premise release of SAP S/4HANA 2022). We’ll also cover
the specific impacts of the simplification items in the relevant chapters; in this section,
we cover the simplification items that aren’t covered in the other chapters.
Embedded PP/DS can’t function as a planning hub. If there are multiple ERP systems,
such as SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, in the solution landscape, the embedded PP/DS of one
SAP S/4HANA system can’t act as a central planning and scheduling system for all the
ERP systems in the landscape. Only the planning data that is part of an SAP S/4HANA
system can be used by embedded PP/DS of the same system. Standalone SAP Advanced
Planning and Optimization systems can work alongside embedded PP/DS, but the data
should be segregated in a way that the same set of data isn’t planned by embedded PP/DS
and the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. A scenario in
which a product location is planned in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization
system for supply network planning and the same product location is planned in
embedded PP/DS isn’t supported in the standard delivered SAP S/4HANA software;
however, custom interfaces may be used to support such a scenario.
Let’s walk through the key simplifications, as follows:
 Production versions
In the SAP ERP system, production-related master data such as BOMs and routings
are created and linked via the master data object called the production version.
These production versions, when transferred to the SAP Advanced Planning and
Optimization systems, are created as production process models (PPMs) or as pro-
duction data structures (PDSs) in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization sys-
tem. While PPMs are based on older data models, PDSs are the new objects that can
replace PPMs in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. However, in the SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization system, both PPMs and PDSs are supported.
© 

31
1.2 PP/DS with SAP
In embedded PP/DS, only PDSs are supported; if you’re using PPMs in your existing
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems and plan to use embedded PP/DS,
the usage of PDSs is mandatory. If you have any enhancements implemented for the
transfer of PPM in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization or SAP ERP sys-
tems, these need to be evaluated and adapted to the enhancements related to PDSs.
We’ll cover this further in Chapter 2.
 Simplified master data maintenance
In SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems, it’s possible for local material
masters and resources within SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization to be used in
the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. However, with
embedded PP/DS, because one of the principal objectives is to reduce data duplication,
it’s not possible to create materials and resources just in PP/DS; instead, the materials
and work centers (resources) should be created in SAP S/4HANA in the corresponding
transactions and should be marked for advanced planning. This will make these mate-
rials and resources available in the PP/DS transaction in the SAP S/4HANA system.
 MRP-based detailed scheduling
In SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, MRP-based detailed scheduling executes
MRP in the ERP system (e.g., SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA), and the PP/DS component of
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization is only used for detailed scheduling features.
The orders created in the ERP system via MRP execution are transferred to the SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization system where the detailed scheduling is per-
formed. After the detailed scheduling step, the new schedule with the new order dates
is transferred back to the ERP system. However, with embedded PP/DS, this MRP-based
detailed scheduling functionality isn’t available. After a material is activated for
advanced planning, it must be planned and scheduled with embedded PP/DS.
 MRP execution
In the planning solution with SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimiza-
tion systems, it’s possible to execute MRP in SAP ERP even though the material is
planned by the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. This
option isn’t available in embedded PP/DS because MRP Live will always plan the
advanced planning materials in PP/DS and not use the MRP algorithm in SAP ERP.
 Planning areas
The demand planning and supply network planning components of the SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization system use a data object called the planning
area. All the demand planning and supply network planning data is stored at the
planning area level. Some PP/DS functionalities, such as deployment planning in
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, use the planning area data object as well.
In embedded PP/DS, the demand planning and supply network planning compo-
nents of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization aren’t available, so the planning
areas concept doesn’t exist in SAP S/4HANA, and the PP/DS component features of

1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA
32
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization that are dependent on the planning area
aren’t available in SAP S/4HANA. Therefore, functionalities such as capacity reserva-
tion and PP/DS deployment aren’t supported in embedded PP/DS.
 Global available-to-promise (global ATP)
Global ATP is a tool in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization that can be trig-
gered during the sales order creation process in the ERP system to check for the
availability of the product and commit an availability date to the sales order. Simi-
larly, capable-to-promise (CTP) is another availability check tool in SAP Advanced
Planning and Optimization that checks for product availability; if there is no avail-
ability, the CTP tool creates a temporary planned order in SAP Advanced Planning
and Optimization by considering the available capacity of the resources and then
proposes an availability date back to the ERP system.
The global ATP and CTP tools aren’t part of embedded PP/DS, so these checks
during the creation of sales orders aren’t available in SAP S/4HANA. However, for
planned orders and production orders, the native available-to-promise (ATP) tool of
SAP S/4HANA is integrated for the availability check of planned and production
order components. If a planned order is created or converted into a production
order in embedded PP/DS, the corresponding order created in SAP S/4HANA trig-
gers the ATP check for the components.
 Custom sort profiles
In the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, the order conversion and
fixed pegging functionalities can use custom sort profiles to define the sequence of
orders using the available order properties. These custom sort profiles are based on
the global ATP functionality. Because global ATP isn’t supported in embedded PP/DS,
the custom sort profiles also aren’t available in SAP S/4HANA.
 Capable-to-match (CTM)
CTM is another tool in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system used to
plan the demands in multiple levels of the supply chain finitely. This tool isn’t part
of SAP S/4HANA because embedded PP/DS is no longer bundled with other SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization components such as demand planning or
supply network planning.
 PP/DS optimizer
The PP/DS optimizer is a powerful scheduling optimizer that creates an optimized
plan according to the objective functions defined for optimization. In the PP/DS
component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, the optimizer can create
new supply elements (e.g., planned orders) if there is a supply shortage. In embedded
PP/DS, on the other hand, the PP/DS optimizer can’t create planned orders; it can
only schedule production orders and planned orders.

 Data
When master data is transferred between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimiza-
tion and the ERP system via the core interface, there are multiple enhancement
options (e.g., user exits and business add-ins [BAdIs]) available to add additional
fields and to enhance the master data. Such enhancements cover material masters
and classification data (classes and characteristics). If these enhancements are used
in the existing SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, you need to adapt
those to the corresponding enhancement options available in the SAP S/4HANA sys-
tem. In embedded PP/DS, you can use the extensibility features to add fields to the
material master so that any additional fields created in SAP Advanced Planning and
Optimization can be made available in the SAP S/4HANA material master.
1.2.3 Deployment
In this section, we’ll cover the deployment options available for PP/DS. To understand
the reduced complexity of the deployment of embedded PP/DS, we’ll discuss the vari-
ous deployment options available for the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Planning
and Optimization and in SAP ERP, add-on for embedded PP/DS.
PP/DS with SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization
When introduced, SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization was a standalone system
on the Basis platform, which is now the SAP NetWeaver platform. The underlying data-
base can be any database system, such as SAP HANA, Oracle, DB2, DB6, or Microsoft SQL
Server (MSSQL). The SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system requires a sepa-
rate database for high-speed processing of the planning component, which is SAP live-
Cache. SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization also supports the optimization of
planning problems, and the optimizer server can be also connected to the SAP Advanced
Planning and Optimization system for executing optimizations in the areas of supply
network planning, CTM, transportation load builder, and PP/DS, among others. The opti-
mizer engine software is installed in a server that is connected to the SAP Advanced Plan-
ning and Optimization system via TCP/IP. The standalone SAP Advanced Planning and
Optimization deployment option is depicted in Figure 1.3.
SAP liveCache in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization is loaded with the time-
series data that is relevant for demand planning and supply network planning, as well
as order data that is used by supply network planning and PP/DS. In addition, SAP live-
Cache has an ATP time-series data object that is used by the Global ATP functionality.
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization also contains a business warehouse envi-
ronment, which is primarily used by the demand planning component of the SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization system to store historical data that is used in the
forecasting process.

1.2.4 Architecture
SAP S/4HANA has a new, simplified architecture to remove any redundancies in tech-
nologies, applications, and data. In this section, we’ll cover the general architecture of
the SAP S/4HANA system and the architecture of embedded PP/DS.
SAP S/4HANA simplified the architecture of the previous ERP versions. The principle of
one is applied in the new architecture, which simplifies any duplicate functionalities
and the need to save the same data in multiple tables for performance purposes. From
a technical perspective, the multiple frameworks available with the ERP systems to
realize functionality have been simplified in SAP S/4HANA.
In the ERP systems running on any database, to optimize the performance of the appli-
cations, the data is aggregated at different characteristics levels of the data, such as
periods (daily, weekly, monthly), and aggregated at certain organizational levels. How-
ever, with the power of SAP HANA, these aggregations can be performed on the fly, and
there is no need to create redundant data in the database tables. With SAP S/4HANA,
the applications can use the SAP HANA database to perform complex calculations. An
example of how the inventory data storage is simplified in the SAP S/4HANA architec-
ture is shown in Figure 1.10. In this example, the data is stored in more than 25 tables in
SAP ERP systems, whereas this is simplified to just 2 tables in the SAP S/4HANA system.

Embedded PP/DS has a simplified master data architecture. The master data is main-
tained in SAP S/4HANA and is visible and available for embedded PP/DS. The material
master and work center are activated for advanced planning, which makes it available
for embedded PP/DS. For the resource master data, the corresponding SAP liveCache
time stream is also generated.
For PP/DS master data, such as the PDS, a generation report is provided, which will gen-
erate and save the PDS in the PP/DS tables by using the remote function call (RFC)
within the same SAP S/4HANA system. The business partner data (customers and ven-
dors) and the organizational structure data (plant, shipping points, and MRP areas) are
transferred to embedded PP/DS using a generation report. The variant configuration
classes created in SAP S/4HANA are available for embedded PP/DS without the need to
create any specific integration model.
For master data elements such as purchase info records, contracts, and scheduling
agreements, an integration model is required to generate the external procurement
relationship master data in embedded PP/DS. In addition, the characteristics-dependent
planning (CDP) class type, which is specific to embedded PP/DS and not relevant for SAP
S/4HANA, also requires an integration model for the transfer to embedded PP/DS.
The transaction data created in SAP S/4HANA is also transferred to embedded PP/DS
and saved in SAP liveCache and in the mapping tables to ensure the consistency of the
data in SAP S/4HANA and SAP liveCache. Similarly, the planning data created in embed-
ded PP/DS is saved in SAP liveCache and sent to SAP S/4HANA. The transaction data
includes planned orders and production orders for in-house manufacturing, purchase
requisitions, purchase orders, scheduling agreement releases for external procure-
ment, sales orders, forecast elements, and PIRs. The data architecture for most com-
monly used master and transaction data is shown in Figure 1.13.

1.3 Summary
In this chapter, we introduced the basics of production planning, detailed scheduling,
and deployment options, as well as the architecture of the PP/DS component for SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization, embedded PP/DS, and the SAP Digital Supply
Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA (specifically, SAP S/4HANA Manufactur-
ing for planning and scheduling) solutions. We also covered the evolution of the PP/DS
architecture in the SAP systems and the embedded PP/DS data architecture in detail.
As we discussed in this chapter, the cloud-based SAP IBP system, embedded PP/DS, and
SAP Digital Supply Chain PP/DS will eventually replace the on-premise SAP Advanced
Planning and Optimization system for the demand, supply planning, and PP/DS func-
tionalities.
In the next chapter, we’ll cover the critical master data objects required to operate
embedded PP/DS for executing the PP/DS processes.
